beats.text: The business pays the NJ tax *for you*
beats.sub: You get a credit on your NJ return.
Every year. It doesn't carry over.

captions.instagram:
Own a New Jersey partnership or S corp? Ask about BAIT before March 15.

✔️ BAIT (Pass-Through Business Alternative Income Tax) lets the business pay the NJ income tax for its owners. Owners get a credit on their NJ returns.
✔️ Partnerships, S corps and LLCs taxed as either can elect. Single-member LLCs and sole proprietors can't.
✔️ It's an annual election: for 2026, by March 15, 2027 for calendar-year businesses.
✔️ Federally, entity-level state tax is deducted by the business instead of counting toward each owner's SALT cap.

Whether it helps depends on your income. Our SALT cap guide covers NJ BAIT and NY PTET.

captions.youtube_description: New Jersey's Pass-Through Business Alternative Income Tax (BAIT) lets a partnership or S corp pay NJ income tax at the entity level; owners get a credit on their NJ returns. Single-member LLCs and sole proprietors can't elect. Elect each year by the original return due date: March 15, 2027 for 2026. Federally, it can work around the SALT cap.

sources.fact: NJ BAIT: partnerships, NJ S corps and LLCs taxed as either may elect; single-member LLCs and sole proprietors can't; annual election by the original return due date (March 15 for calendar-year filers); members get a refundable credit (page updated 04/16/26); read 2026-10-30

Notice 2020-75: entity-level state income tax payments by a partnership or S corporation are deductible by the entity and not taken into account in applying the SALT limitation to owners; read 2026-10-30
